entries.proposition: COHORT: 23 consecutive patients with oral leukoplakia, 14 M / 9 F, 29-67 y, 19 smokers. DATO.
entries.snippet: Fresh tissue samples were consecutively obtained from 23 patients (14 males and nine females; age ranged from 29 to 67 years, mean 47 years;
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Human tissue, sentence 1

entries.proposition: CONTROLS: normal mucosa from volunteers; their NUMBER IS NOT STATED anywhere in the paper. DATO.
entries.snippet: Normal oral mucosa was obtained from volunteers without leukoplakia during non-neoplastic or preprosthetic surgical procedures (control samples).
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Human tissue, sentence 3

entries.proposition: RNA FROM MICRODISSECTED LESIONS. DATO.
entries.snippet: treated with DNAse (Invitrogen Life Technologies, Carlsbad, CA), after microdissection.
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Reverse transcription-PCR analysis, sentence 1

entries.proposition: NESTED RT-PCR as in ref 28 (two rounds of 35 cycles each, second round seeded with 1 ul of the first). DATO. As in the 2006 OSCC paper, 70 cycles on small microdissected inputs makes artefactual junction products possible, and none is excluded (INFERENZA, reader).
entries.snippet: The first and second amplifications were performed with nested primers as previously described.
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Reverse transcription-PCR analysis

entries.proposition: TWO PRODUCTS SEQUENCED PER CASE. DATO.
entries.snippet: To each case, two different amplified products were sequenced.
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Reverse transcription-PCR analysis, last sentence

entries.proposition: ANTISERUM as in ref 30 (Ludes-Meyers 2003), 140 ug/ml at 1:100. DATO.
entries.snippet: Primary polyclonal rabbit antiWwox antiserum (140 μg/ml) was used at a 1:100 dilution

entries.proposition: IHC SCORE BY EXTENT: +1 0-50%, +2 51-75%, +3 >76%; +3 = normal. DATO. THE SAME GROUP, SAME ANTISERUM AND SAME PROTOCOL used +1 0-10%, +2 11-50%, +3 >50% for OSCC in 2006, so a '+2' here and a '+2' there are different quantities; and the scale leaves 75-76% undefined.
entries.snippet: Two experienced independent pathologists examined multiple fields and scored tissue sections for extent of staining, regardless of staining intensity (+1, 0–50% positive cells; +2, 51–75% positive cells; +3, greater than 76% positive cells).

entries.proposition: TABLE 1 FOOTNOTE repeats the thresholds. DATO.
entries.snippet: +1, 0–50% positive cells; +2, 51–75% positive cells; +3, >76% positive cells.

entries.proposition: TRANSCRIPT ALTERATION: 6/23 (26%). DATO.
entries.snippet: six of 23 cases (26%) showed altered or absent expression of WWOX gene transcription.
entries.anchor: Results > Aberrant WWOX gene transcripts, sentence 1

experimental_context.system: human tissue, oral leukoplakia (23 lesions) and normal oral mucosa

entries.proposition: OL2 PRODUCT: partial exon 2, exons 3-6 lost, partial exon 7. DATO. The junction joins two exon interiors, not exon boundaries, so it is not a canonical splice product; genomic DNA was not analysed in this paper (INFERENZA, reader).
entries.snippet: Sequence analyses of the RT-PCR products showed partial loss of exon 2, total loss of exons 3–6 and partial loss of exon 7 (#OL2) (Fig. 1b)
entries.anchor: Results > Aberrant WWOX gene transcripts, sentence 4

experimental_context.system: human tissue, oral leukoplakia (23 lesions) and normal oral mucosa

entries.proposition: OL23: two aberrant products, one internal partial-exon deletion (partial exon 1 to partial exon 8) and one clean exon 6-8 skip (Delta6-8). DATO.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, two transcript variants were present in lesion #OL23, one with partial loss of exon 1, total loss of exons 2–7 and partial loss of 8 in one (Fig. 1e) and the other with loss of exons 6–8 (Fig. 1f).

entries.snippet: In case #OL16 we detected a band of abnormal size and we sequenced the exons 1–6 and part of exon 7 but the aberrant transcript was not possible detected because of minute sample amount.

Schematics b-f: OL2 1-2*-7*-8-9; OL14 1*-7*-8-9; OL18 1-2*-8*-9; OL23(<) 1*-8*-9; OL23(>) 1-2-3-4-5-9. Consistent with the Results text.

entries.snippet: Of the 23 OLs, six lesions (26%) showed a reduced expression to Wwox.

entries.proposition: CAPTION 2A: normal mucosa with '(strong)' cytoplasmic staining. DATO as printed.
entries.snippet: (a) Normal oral mucosa showing (strong) cytoplasmic staining in all layers of the epithelium (score +3).

entries.proposition: FIGURE 2, NATIVE PIXELS (1608x389, three panels). a normal mucosa: diffuse PALE brown cytoplasmic staining - moderate at most, not strong; b #OL10: similar pale-brown; c #OL2: epithelium unstained with a few brown elongated cells between keratinocytes. Scoring is by extent so intensity does not enter the score, but the caption's '(strong)' is not what the panel shows.

entries.proposition: COMBINED: 35% of lesions altered; 4/6 transcript-altered lesions have reduced protein, called 'significant' without a test. DATO for the counts.
entries.snippet: the results obtained by RT-PCR and immunohistochemistry showed that 35% of the lesions presented mRNA and/or protein alteration and the majority of lesions (4/6) with altered transcripts had a significant reduction in the expression of Wwox protein (Table 1).
entries.anchor: Results > Expression of Wwox protein, last sentence

entries.proposition: DYSPLASIA: altered in 5/11 moderate-severe, 3/8 mild, 0/4 no dysplasia. DATO; counts reproduce exactly from Table 1. No test is reported; recomputed two-sided Fisher any-dysplasia vs none p=0.26, moderate-severe vs mild-or-none p=0.40. The 'none of the four without dysplasia' rests on n=4.
entries.snippet: While five out of the 11 samples with moderate or severe dysplasia showed WWOX alteration, three out of eight lesions with mild dysplasia and none of the four cases without dysplasia presented this alteration.
entries.anchor: Results > Correlation between the presence of dysplasia and WWOX alteration

entries.proposition: SPLICING-ERROR RATIONALE: 'very long transcripts such as WWOX' (ref 30). The WWOX GENE spans a very long genomic region; its mature coding transcript is not long (the paper itself amplifies a 1284 bp product). A conflation of gene length with transcript length, in the authors' text.
entries.snippet: Furthermore, the splicing abnormalities would more often affect genes that have very long transcripts such as WWOX.

entries.proposition: THE HEADLINE SENTENCE says 'with WWOX mRNA and/or protein expression' where 'alteration' is meant; the same wording is in the abstract. DATO as printed.
entries.snippet: all lesions with WWOX mRNA and/or protein expression showed histological evidence of dysplasia and none of the cases without dysplasia presented this alteration.

entries.proposition: 'EARLY GENETIC ALTERATION ... could contribute to oral carcinogenesis': cross-sectional, no follow-up to malignant transformation, no genomic DNA analysis. IPOTESI stated as a result.
entries.snippet: These results show that the WWOX gene alteration is an early genetic alteration that could contribute to oral carcinogenesis
